dct_description_sm: Along the entire Hershel Island coast, the amount of retrogressive thaw slumps has approximately doubled since the mid-twentieth century. Hence, the risk of accelerated permafrost degradation due to climate warming is evident. In this study, we present information on former thaw slump transitions (active to stabilized states), current thermokarst retreat rates, as well as predictions on how modern slumps might evolve when they approach previous stabilized headwalls. An improved understanding of retrogressive thaw slump evolution is important for assessing the potential impacts of a warmer Arctic on the islands natural and cultural resources.
dct_title_s: Biogeophysical Characterization of Polycyclic Thermokarst on Herschel Island, Yukon Territory
